mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (indicating monetary easing) compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.10%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment (UNRATE below 3.5%) signals a tight labor market that supports strong corporate profit growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is below 3.5%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Strong consumer demand is indicated by concurrent growth in employment (PAYEMS) and retail sales (RSAFS), which drives corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS and RSAFS growth both exceed 0.5%, SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression has a negative coefficient and is significant.

mechanism_narrative: In early-cycle expansion, rising industrial production (INDPRO) signals strengthening manufacturing activity and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In early-cycle expansion periods, INDPRO growth exceeding 0.5% leads to negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: High housing starts (HOUST above 1000.0 thousand units) indicate robust consumer confidence and economic activity, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST exceeds 1000.0, SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates a robust economy that supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 quarterly growth rate exceeds 2.0%, SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) combined with a falling federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals coordinated monetary and labor market policy easing, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary easing with labor market softening
failure_condition: When UNRATE is below 6.5% and FEDFUNDS is below 0.10%, SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression is not significant and positive.

mechanism_narrative: In a high inflation regime (CPIAUCSL YoY growth above 2.5%), the S&P 500 tends to experience negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve.
failure_condition: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL YoY growth > 2.5%), SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
